Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak marched to Hansi, forcing Jatwan to retreat to Bagar, where the rebel was defeated and killed in a battle. The above-mentioned information about Jatwan's rebellion comes from the contemporary writer Hasan Nizami.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The above-mentioned information about Jatwan's rebellion comes from the contemporary writer _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The above-mentioned information about Jatwan's rebellion comes from the contemporary writer Hasan Nizami.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to _____, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of Gujarat after his defeat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to 1203, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of Gujarat after his defeat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He was later killed as a subordinate of the _____ king Bhima II when Aibak invaded Gujarat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He was later killed as a subordinate of the Chaulukya king Bhima II when Aibak invaded Gujarat. Historian A.K. Majumdar adds that Firishta may have confused the Chaulukya ruler Bhima with Bhima-simha, who - according to the Kharatara Gaccha Pattavali - was the governor of Hansi in 1171 CE.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to historian _____, Firishta may have confused the Bagar tract (where Jatwan was killed) with another area called Bagar near the Gujarat border, around Banswara and Dungarpur
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to historian Dasharatha Sharma, Firishta may have confused the Bagar tract (where Jatwan was killed) with another area called Bagar near the Gujarat border, around Banswara and Dungarpur.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Historian A.K. Majumdar adds that Firishta may have confused the Chaulukya ruler Bhima with Bhima-simha, who - according to the Kharatara Gaccha Pattavali - was the governor of Hansi in _____ CE
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Historian A.K. Majumdar adds that Firishta may have confused the Chaulukya ruler Bhima with Bhima-simha, who - according to the Kharatara Gaccha Pattavali - was the governor of Hansi in 1171 CE.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Thus, _____ may have been a general of Bhima-simha, and may have tried to recover the fort on behalf of his master
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to historian Dasharatha Sharma, Firishta may have confused the Bagar tract (where Jatwan was killed) with another area called Bagar near the Gujarat border, around Banswara and Dungarpur. Thus, Jatwan may have been a general of Bhima-simha, and may have tried to recover the fort on behalf of his master.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Nizami does not state this, and _____'s guess appears to be based on the similarity of the words "Jatwan" and "Jat", and the rebellion's locality, where Jats can be found
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Nizami does not state this, and Elliot's guess appears to be based on the similarity of the words "Jatwan" and "Jat", and the rebellion's locality, where Jats can be found.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to S.H. _____, "Jatwan" is a mistranscription of the "Chahwan" in the manuscript, and the rebel was probably a Chahamana (Chawhan or Chauhan) subordinate of Prithivraja
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to S.H. Hodivala, "Jatwan" is a mistranscription of the "Chahwan" in the manuscript, and the rebel was probably a Chahamana (Chawhan or Chauhan) subordinate of Prithivraja.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, it is probably a corrupt form of the name "Jaitra"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Rima Hooja, it is probably a corrupt form of the name "Jaitra".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1192, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom. He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He also took control of Delhi in _____, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1192, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom. He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1193, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The near-contemporary chronicler _____ does not elaborate why, but the 14th-century chronicler Isami claims that some people had aroused the Sultan's suspicion about Aibak's loyalty
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The near-contemporary chronicler Minhaj does not elaborate why, but the 14th-century chronicler Isami claims that some people had aroused the Sultan's suspicion about Aibak's loyalty.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Historian K. A. Nizami finds Isami's account unreliable and theorizes that the _____ may have sought Aibak's help in planning further Ghurid expansion in India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The near-contemporary chronicler Minhaj does not elaborate why, but the 14th-century chronicler Isami claims that some people had aroused the Sultan's suspicion about Aibak's loyalty. Historian K. A. Nizami finds Isami's account unreliable and theorizes that the Sultan may have sought Aibak's help in planning further Ghurid expansion in India.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his return to India in _____, he crossed the Yamuna River, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his return to India in 1194, he crossed the Yamuna River, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, taking advantage of Aibak's absence in India, _____ had regained control of a part of the former Chahamana territory
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, taking advantage of Aibak's absence in India, Hariraja had regained control of a part of the former Chahamana territory. After his return to Delhi, Aibak sent an army against Hariraja, who committed suicide when faced with certain defeat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his return to Delhi, Aibak sent an army against _____, who committed suicide when faced with certain defeat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, taking advantage of Aibak's absence in India, Hariraja had regained control of a part of the former Chahamana territory. After his return to Delhi, Aibak sent an army against Hariraja, who committed suicide when faced with certain defeat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak subsequently placed Ajmer under a Muslim governor and moved _____ to Ranthambore
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak subsequently placed Ajmer under a Muslim governor and moved Govindaraja to Ranthambore.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After the battle, _____ continued his advance to the east, with Aibek in the vanguard
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After the battle, Muhammad Ghori continued his advance to the east, with Aibek in the vanguard.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Although the _____ did not gain complete control over the Gahadavala kingdom, the victory provided an opportunity for them to establish military stations at many places in the region
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Although the Ghurids did not gain complete control over the Gahadavala kingdom, the victory provided an opportunity for them to establish military stations at many places in the region.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Muhammad Ghori returned to Ghazni but came back to India in _____–96 when he defeated Kumarapala, the Bhati ruler of Bayana
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Muhammad Ghori returned to Ghazni but came back to India in 1195–96 when he defeated Kumarapala, the Bhati ruler of Bayana.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He then marched towards _____, where the local Parihara ruler Sallakhanapala acknowledged his suzerainty after a long siege
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He then marched towards Gwalior, where the local Parihara ruler Sallakhanapala acknowledged his suzerainty after a long siege.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the _____ rule
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Although the Ghurids did not gain complete control over the Gahadavala kingdom, the victory provided an opportunity for them to establish military stations at many places in the region. Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the Ghurid rule.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Supported by the _____, who ruled Gujarat in the south, the Mhers posed a serious threat to Aibak's control of the region
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Supported by the Chaulukyas, who ruled Gujarat in the south, the Mhers posed a serious threat to Aibak's control of the region.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak marched against them but was forced to retreat to _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the Ghurid rule. Aibak marched against them but was forced to retreat to Ajmer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The Mhers were forced to retreat after reinforcements from the _____ capital of Ghazni arrived in Ajmer
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, the Mher tribals, who lived near Ajmer, rebelled against the Ghurid rule. The Mhers were forced to retreat after reinforcements from the Ghurid capital of Ghazni arrived in Ajmer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, Aibak defeated the Chaulukya army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1197, Aibak defeated the Chaulukya army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak's army then marched to the _____ capital Anhilwara: the defending king Bhima II fled the city, which was plundered by the invaders
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1197, Aibak defeated the Chaulukya army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier. Aibak's army then marched to the Chaulukya capital Anhilwara: the defending king Bhima II fled the city, which was plundered by the invaders.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Minhaj characterizes Aibak's raid of _____ as the "conquest of Gujarat", but it did not result in the annexation of Gujarat to the Ghurid Empire
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak's army then marched to the Chaulukya capital Anhilwara: the defending king Bhima II fled the city, which was plundered by the invaders. Minhaj characterizes Aibak's raid of Anhilwara as the "conquest of Gujarat", but it did not result in the annexation of Gujarat to the Ghurid Empire.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Whatever the case, _____ control of the region did not last long, and the Chaulukyas regained control of their capital soon after
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Minhaj characterizes Aibak's raid of Anhilwara as the "conquest of Gujarat", but it did not result in the annexation of Gujarat to the Ghurid Empire. The 16th-century historian Firishta states that Aibak appointed a Muslim officer to consolidate Ghurid power in the region, while Ibn-i Asir states that Aibak placed the newly-captured territory under Hindu vassals.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____–98, Aibak conquered Budaun in present-day Uttar Pradesh, and also re-took control of the former Gahadavala capital Varanasi, which had slipped out of Ghurid control
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1197–98, Aibak conquered Budaun in present-day Uttar Pradesh, and also re-took control of the former Gahadavala capital Varanasi, which had slipped out of Ghurid control.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____–99, he captured Chantarwal (unidentified, possibly the same as Chandawar) and Kannauj
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1198–99, he captured Chantarwal (unidentified, possibly the same as Chandawar) and Kannauj.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Later, he captured Siroh (possibly modern Sirohi in _____)
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Later, he captured Siroh (possibly modern Sirohi in Rajasthan).

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to the _____ chronicler Fakhr-i Mudabbir (c
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to the Persian chronicler Fakhr-i Mudabbir (c.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: _____–1236), Aibak also conquered Malwa in present-day Madhya Pradesh, in 1199–1200
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: 1157–1236), Aibak also conquered Malwa in present-day Madhya Pradesh, in 1199–1200.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: However, no other historian refers to such a conquest; therefore, it is likely that Aibak merely raided _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: 1157–1236), Aibak also conquered Malwa in present-day Madhya Pradesh, in 1199–1200. However, no other historian refers to such a conquest; therefore, it is likely that Aibak merely raided Malwa.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, Baha' al-_____ (also transliterated as Bahauddin Tughril) - another prominent Ghurid slave-general - besieged the Gwalior Fort
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, Baha' al-Din Toghril (also transliterated as Bahauddin Tughril) - another prominent Ghurid slave-general - besieged the Gwalior Fort.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, Aibak besieged Kalinjar, an important fort in the Chandela kingdom of central India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1202, Aibak besieged Kalinjar, an important fort in the Chandela kingdom of central India.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The Chandela ruler _____ initiated negotiations with Aibak but died before a treaty could be finalized
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Chandela ruler Paramardi initiated negotiations with Aibak but died before a treaty could be finalized.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The Chandela chief minister _____ resumed hostilities but was forced to seek negotiations when the Ghurids cut off the water supply to the fort
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Chandela chief minister Ajayadeva resumed hostilities but was forced to seek negotiations when the Ghurids cut off the water supply to the fort.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: As part of the truce, the _____ were forced to move to Ajaigarh
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: As part of the truce, the Chandelas were forced to move to Ajaigarh.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Their former strongholds of _____, Mahoba, and Khajuraho came under Ghurid control, governed by Hasan Arnal
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Their former strongholds of Kalinjar, Mahoba, and Khajuraho came under Ghurid control, governed by Hasan Arnal. After his Bihar campaign, which involved the destruction of Buddhist monasteries, Khalji arrived in Badaun to greet Aibak, who had just concluded his successful campaign at Kalinjar.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, the _____ commander Bakhtiyar Khalji subjugated the petty Gahadavala chiefs in eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Bihar region
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Chandela chief minister Ajayadeva resumed hostilities but was forced to seek negotiations when the Ghurids cut off the water supply to the fort. Their former strongholds of Kalinjar, Mahoba, and Khajuraho came under Ghurid control, governed by Hasan Arnal.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his Bihar campaign, which involved the destruction of _____ monasteries, Khalji arrived in Badaun to greet Aibak, who had just concluded his successful campaign at Kalinjar
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his Bihar campaign, which involved the destruction of Buddhist monasteries, Khalji arrived in Badaun to greet Aibak, who had just concluded his successful campaign at Kalinjar.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: On 23 March _____, Khalji presented Aibak with war booty, including 20 captured elephants, jewels, and cash
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: On 23 March 1203, Khalji presented Aibak with war booty, including 20 captured elephants, jewels, and cash.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak honoured _____, who went on to conquer a part of the Bengal region in the east
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, the Ghurid commander Bakhtiyar Khalji subjugated the petty Gahadavala chiefs in eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Bihar region. After his Bihar campaign, which involved the destruction of Buddhist monasteries, Khalji arrived in Badaun to greet Aibak, who had just concluded his successful campaign at Kalinjar.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Bakhtiyar acted independently, and at the time of his death in _____, was not a subordinate of Aibak
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Bakhtiyar acted independently, and at the time of his death in 1206, was not a subordinate of Aibak. On 15 March 1206, Muhammad Ghori was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: On 15 March _____, Muhammad Ghori was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Bakhtiyar acted independently, and at the time of his death in 1206, was not a subordinate of Aibak. On 15 March 1206, Muhammad Ghori was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, Muhammad Ghori suffered a defeat against the Khwarazmians and their allies at the Battle of Andkhud, followed by several challenges to his authority
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1204, Muhammad Ghori suffered a defeat against the Khwarazmians and their allies at the Battle of Andkhud, followed by several challenges to his authority.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak helped him suppress a rebellion by the _____ chiefs of the Lahore region, and then returned to Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak helped him suppress a rebellion by the Khokhar chiefs of the Lahore region, and then returned to Delhi. On 15 March 1206, Muhammad Ghori was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Minhaj states that at the time of Sultan Muhammad Ghori's death in _____, the Ghurids controlled the following areas in India: However, Ghurid control was not equally effective in all these areas
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: On 15 March 1206, Muhammad Ghori was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis. Minhaj states that at the time of Sultan Muhammad Ghori's death in 1206, the Ghurids controlled the following areas in India: However, Ghurid control was not equally effective in all these areas.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Bakhtiyar was killed by his subordinate Ali Mardan Khalji at Devkot in _____, around the same time Sultan Muhammad Ghori was assassinated
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: On 15 March 1206, Muhammad Ghori was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis. Minhaj states that at the time of Sultan Muhammad Ghori's death in 1206, the Ghurids controlled the following areas in India: However, Ghurid control was not equally effective in all these areas.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In some of these places, such as _____ and Kalinjar, Ghurid control had weakened or even ceased to exist
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In some of these places, such as Gwalior and Kalinjar, Ghurid control had weakened or even ceased to exist.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Subsequently, _____, another subordinate of Bakhtiyar, detained Ali Mardan and became the leader of the Khaljis in eastern India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Subsequently, Muhammad Shiran Khalji, another subordinate of Bakhtiyar, detained Ali Mardan and became the leader of the Khaljis in eastern India.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The Khaljis were not slaves of _____, so Aibak had no legal authority in the matter
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Bakhtiyar was killed by his subordinate Ali Mardan Khalji at Devkot in 1206, around the same time Sultan Muhammad Ghori was assassinated. The Khaljis were not slaves of Muhammad Ghori, so Aibak had no legal authority in the matter.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Nevertheless, he instructed his subordinate _____ – the governor of Awadh – to march to Lakhnauti in Bengal, and assign suitable iqta's to the Khalji amirs
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Nevertheless, he instructed his subordinate Qaimaz Rumi – the governor of Awadh – to march to Lakhnauti in Bengal, and assign suitable iqta's to the Khalji amirs. Qaimaz Rumi assigned the iqta' of Devkot to Husamuddin Iwaz Khalji, another subordinate of Bakhtiyar.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Qaimaz Rumi assigned the iqta' of Devkot to _____, another subordinate of Bakhtiyar
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Qaimaz Rumi assigned the iqta' of Devkot to Husamuddin Iwaz Khalji, another subordinate of Bakhtiyar.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Muhammad Shiran and other _____ amirs disagreed with this decision and marched to Devkot
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The Khaljis were not slaves of Muhammad Ghori, so Aibak had no legal authority in the matter. Nevertheless, he instructed his subordinate Qaimaz Rumi – the governor of Awadh – to march to Lakhnauti in Bengal, and assign suitable iqta's to the Khalji amirs.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: However, Rumi defeated them decisively, and _____ was later killed in a conflict
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Muhammad Shiran and other Khalji amirs disagreed with this decision and marched to Devkot. However, Rumi defeated them decisively, and Shiran was later killed in a conflict.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Hasan Nizami also states that the iyalat (governorship) of _____ and Samana was entrusted to Aibak
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Hasan Nizami also states that the iyalat (governorship) of Kuhram and Samana was entrusted to Aibak.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Fakhr-i Mudabbir, another contemporary chronicler, states that Muhammad Ghori formally appointed Aibak as the viceroy of his Indian territories only in _____ when he was returning to Ghazni after supp
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Fakhr-i Mudabbir, another contemporary chronicler, states that Muhammad Ghori formally appointed Aibak as the viceroy of his Indian territories only in 1206 when he was returning to Ghazni after suppressing the Khokhar rebellion.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to this chronicler, Aibak was promoted to the rank of malik and appointed heir apparent (wali al-ahd) of the _____'s Indian territories
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to this chronicler, Aibak was promoted to the rank of malik and appointed heir apparent (wali al-ahd) of the Sultan's Indian territories. Historian K. A. Nizami theorizes that Sultan Muhammad Ghori never appointed Aibak as his successor in India: the slave-general acquired this position after the Sultan's death through the use of diplomacy and military power.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: During his last years, the _____ was disappointed in his family and his chiefs and trusted only his slaves, whom he thought of as his sons and successors
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to this chronicler, Aibak was promoted to the rank of malik and appointed heir apparent (wali al-ahd) of the Sultan's Indian territories. Historian K. A. Nizami theorizes that Sultan Muhammad Ghori never appointed Aibak as his successor in India: the slave-general acquired this position after the Sultan's death through the use of diplomacy and military power.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: At the time of the _____'s death, Aibak had his headquarters at Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Historian K. A. Nizami theorizes that Sultan Muhammad Ghori never appointed Aibak as his successor in India: the slave-general acquired this position after the Sultan's death through the use of diplomacy and military power. The Sultan's unexpected death left three of his main slave-generals – Aibak, Taj al-Din Yildiz, and Nasir ad-Din Qabacha – in positions of power.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The citizens of _____ requested him to assume sovereign power after the Sultan's death, and he moved his government to Lahore
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The citizens of Lahore requested him to assume sovereign power after the Sultan's death, and he moved his government to Lahore.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He informally ascended the throne on 25 June _____, but his formal recognition as a sovereign ruler happened much later, in 1208–1209
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He informally ascended the throne on 25 June 1206, but his formal recognition as a sovereign ruler happened much later, in 1208–1209.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, in and around _____, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, in and around Ghazni, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: When Mahmud had consolidated his rule, Aibak and other slaves sent messengers to his court, seeking deeds of manumission and investiture for ruling over the various _____ territories
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, in and around Ghazni, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne. When Mahmud had consolidated his rule, Aibak and other slaves sent messengers to his court, seeking deeds of manumission and investiture for ruling over the various Ghurid territories.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Yildiz, who was Aibak's father-in-law, sought to control the _____ territories in India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, in and around Ghazni, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne. When Mahmud had consolidated his rule, Aibak and other slaves sent messengers to his court, seeking deeds of manumission and investiture for ruling over the various Ghurid territories.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Aibak (unlike Yildiz) maintained the khutba and struck coins in Mahmud's name
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak (unlike Yildiz) maintained the khutba and struck coins in Mahmud's name.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After Sultan Mahmud confirmed him as the ruler of _____ and manumitted him, Yildiz marched to Punjab, intending to take control of the region
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After Sultan Mahmud confirmed him as the ruler of Ghazni and manumitted him, Yildiz marched to Punjab, intending to take control of the region. Aibak marched against him, forced him to retreat to Kohistan, and took control of Ghazni.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak marched against him, forced him to retreat to _____, and took control of Ghazni
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak marched against him, forced him to retreat to Kohistan, and took control of Ghazni.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak then sent his representative _____ to Mahmud's headquarters at Firuz Kuh, seeking to expedite his request for the investiture
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak then sent his representative Nizamuddin Muhammad to Mahmud's headquarters at Firuz Kuh, seeking to expedite his request for the investiture.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____–1209, Mahmud conferred a chatr (ceremonial parasol) on Aibak, and issued a deed of investiture recognizing him as the ruler of Hindustan
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1208–1209, Mahmud conferred a chatr (ceremonial parasol) on Aibak, and issued a deed of investiture recognizing him as the ruler of Hindustan.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to Minhaj's _____-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj's Tabaqat-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: No coins issued by him have been found, and no extant coins describe him as a "_____"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj's Tabaqat-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan". No coins issued by him have been found, and no extant coins describe him as a "Sultan".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj's Tabaqat-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan". According to Minhaj, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The people of _____ invited Yildiz to evict him from the city, and when Yildiz arrived in the vicinity of Ghazni, Aibak panicked and escaped to India via a narrow mountain pass called Sang-i Surkh
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni. The people of Ghazni invited Yildiz to evict him from the city, and when Yildiz arrived in the vicinity of Ghazni, Aibak panicked and escaped to India via a narrow mountain pass called Sang-i Surkh.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Ali Mardan Khalji, who had accompanied Aibak to _____, was captured and imprisoned by Yildiz
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni. The people of Ghazni invited Yildiz to evict him from the city, and when Yildiz arrived in the vicinity of Ghazni, Aibak panicked and escaped to India via a narrow mountain pass called Sang-i Surkh.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak dispatched him to _____ in Bengal, where Husamuddin Iwaz agreed to be his subordinate
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak dispatched him to Lakhnauti in Bengal, where Husamuddin Iwaz agreed to be his subordinate.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, he fell down from a horse while playing chaugan (a form of polo on horseback) in Lahore, and died instantly when the pommel of the saddle pierced his ribs
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1210, he fell down from a horse while playing chaugan (a form of polo on horseback) in Lahore, and died instantly when the pommel of the saddle pierced his ribs.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, his generosity earned him the epithet lakh-bakhsh, literally "giver of lakhs [of copper coins or jitals]"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, his generosity earned him the epithet lakh-bakhsh, literally "giver of lakhs [of copper coins or jitals]".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The 16th century _____ chronicler Abu'l-Fazl criticizes Mahmud of Ghazna for "shedding innocent blood", but praises Aibak stating that "he achieved things, good and great"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The 16th century Mughal chronicler Abu'l-Fazl criticizes Mahmud of Ghazna for "shedding innocent blood", but praises Aibak stating that "he achieved things, good and great".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: As late as the 17th century, the term "Aibak of the time" was used to describe generous people, as attested by the chronicler _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: As late as the 17th century, the term "Aibak of the time" was used to describe generous people, as attested by the chronicler Firishta.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, his Gujarat campaign resulted in the enslavement of 20,000 people; and his Kalinjar campaign resulted in the enslavement of 50,000 people
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Hasan Nizami, his Gujarat campaign resulted in the enslavement of 20,000 people; and his Kalinjar campaign resulted in the enslavement of 50,000 people.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Nizami's work is full of rhetoric and hyperbole, so these numbers seem to be exaggerated, however, the number of slaves collected must indeed have been vast and grew over time
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Irfan Habib, Nizami's work is full of rhetoric and hyperbole, so these numbers seem to be exaggerated, however, the number of slaves collected must indeed have been vast and grew over time.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his death, the _____ officers (maliks and umara) stationed at Lahore appointed Aram Shah as his successor
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his death, the Turkic officers (maliks and umara) stationed at Lahore appointed Aram Shah as his successor. Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave Iltutmish, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: No details about _____'s life are available before his ascension to the throne
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his death, the Turkic officers (maliks and umara) stationed at Lahore appointed Aram Shah as his successor. No details about Aram Shah's life are available before his ascension to the throne.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave _____, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave Iltutmish, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom. Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Aibak looked upon Iltutmish as the next ruler: he used to call Iltutmish his son and had granted him the iqta' of Badaun
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak looked upon Iltutmish as the next ruler: he used to call Iltutmish his son and had granted him the iqta' of Badaun.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Consequently, the nobles appointed Iltutmish as _____'s successor and married Aibak's daughter to him
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Consequently, the nobles appointed Iltutmish as Aram Shah's successor and married Aibak's daughter to him. Aram Shah challenged Iltutmish's claim to the throne but was decisively defeated and killed after a military conflict.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aram Shah challenged _____'s claim to the throne but was decisively defeated and killed after a military conflict
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197. According to Minhaj, Aibak looked upon Iltutmish as the next ruler: he used to call Iltutmish his son and had granted him the iqta' of Badaun.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Iltutmish subjugated the rebel governors and transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Iltutmish subjugated the rebel governors and transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful Delhi Sultanate.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Iltutmish was succeeded by his family members, and then by his slave _____ ud din Balban
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Iltutmish was succeeded by his family members, and then by his slave Ghiyas ud din Balban.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: This line of kings is called _____ or Slave dynasty; however, this term is a misnomer
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: This line of kings is called Mamluk or Slave dynasty; however, this term is a misnomer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Only Aibak, _____, and Balban were slaves, and seem to have been manumitted before their ascension to the throne
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Iltutmish subjugated the rebel governors and transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful Delhi Sultanate. Iltutmish was succeeded by his family members, and then by his slave Ghiyas ud din Balban.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Today his tomb is located in _____, Lahore
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Today his tomb is in Anarkali, Lahore.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the _____ of Archaeology and Museums (Pakistan) which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the Department of Archaeology and Museums (Pakistan) which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Before the modern construction, the _____'s grave existed in a simple form and was enclosed by residential houses
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the Department of Archaeology and Museums (Pakistan) which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture. Before the modern construction, the Sultan's grave existed in a simple form and was enclosed by residential houses.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Historians dispute whether a proper tomb ever existed over it (some historians claim that a marble dome did stand over it but was destroyed by the _____)
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Historians dispute whether a proper tomb ever existed over it (some historians claim that a marble dome did stand over it but was destroyed by the Sikhs).

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: However, this may have been an erroneous addition made by a careless scribe, as _____-i-Juwayni's Tarikh-i-Jahan-Gusha chronicle explicitly mentions that Aibak had no son
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: However, this may have been an erroneous addition made by a careless scribe, as Alauddin Ata Malik-i-Juwayni's Tarikh-i-Jahan-Gusha chronicle explicitly mentions that Aibak had no son.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Contrarily, the 14th century historian _____ stated Aaram Shah as Aibak's real son
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Contrarily, the 14th century historian Abdul Malik Isami stated Aaram Shah as Aibak's real son.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The first one was married to Nasir ad-_____, the Ghurid governor of Multan
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The first one was married to Nasir ad-Din Qabacha, the Ghurid governor of Multan.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After her death, the second daughter was married to _____ as well
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The first one was married to Nasir ad-Din Qabacha, the Ghurid governor of Multan. After her death, the second daughter was married to Qabacha as well.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The third one was married to Aibak's slave Iltutmish, who succeeded _____ on the throne of Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The third one was married to Aibak's slave Iltutmish, who succeeded Aram Shah on the throne of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He also mentions that the Hindu temples at Meerut and _____ were converted into mosques during Aibak's reign; these included "a thousand temples" in Delhi alone
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He also mentions that the Hindu temples at Meerut and Kalinjar were converted into mosques during Aibak's reign; these included "a thousand temples" in Delhi alone.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He further claims that Aibak freed the whole Kol (_____) region from idols and idolatry
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He further claims that Aibak freed the whole Kol (Aligarh) region from idols and idolatry.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: At some point, Aibak's army started recruiting _____ soldiers
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Nizami's claim that the remains of the demolished Hindu temples were used to build mosques is corroborated by architectural remains, such as those at the Qutb Minar complex in Delhi and the Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra in Ajmer. At some point, Aibak's army started recruiting Hindu soldiers.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: His army at the siege of Meerut (_____) is known to have included Hindu soldiers
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: His army at the siege of Meerut (1192) is known to have included Hindu soldiers.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Similarly, the "forces of Hindustan" (Hasham-i Hindustan) that accompanied him to Ghazni in _____, included Hindu chiefs ("ranas" and "thakurs")
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Similarly, the "forces of Hindustan" (Hasham-i Hindustan) that accompanied him to Ghazni in 1206, included Hindu chiefs ("ranas" and "thakurs").

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The composition of _____'s Tajul-Ma'asir, which was completed during the reign of Iltutmish, probably began during Aibak's reign
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The composition of Hasan Nizami's Tajul-Ma'asir, which was completed during the reign of Iltutmish, probably began during Aibak's reign.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After the _____ victory in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, Muhammad Ghori made Aibak in charge of his Indian territories
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: During the Khwarazmian-Ghurid wars, he was captured by the scouts of Sultan Shah; after the Ghurid victory, he was released and highly favoured by Muhammad Ghori. After the Ghurid victory in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, Muhammad Ghori made Aibak in charge of his Indian territories.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After the assassination of _____ in March 1206, Aibak fought with another former slave-general Taj al-Din Yildiz for control of Ghurid territories in north-western India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: During the Khwarazmian-Ghurid wars, he was captured by the scouts of Sultan Shah; after the Ghurid victory, he was released and highly favoured by Muhammad Ghori. After the Ghurid victory in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, Muhammad Ghori made Aibak in charge of his Indian territories.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: No information is available about Aibak's subsequent assignments until the _____ of Tarain fought in India, in 1191–1192
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: No information is available about Aibak's subsequent assignments until the First Battle of Tarain fought in India, in 1191–1192.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his return to India in 1194, he crossed the _____, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his return to India in 1194, he crossed the Yamuna River, and captured Koil (modern Aligarh) from the Dor Rajputs.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: 1157–1236), Aibak also conquered Malwa in present-day _____, in 1199–1200
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: 1157–1236), Aibak also conquered Malwa in present-day Madhya Pradesh, in 1199–1200.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: On 23 March 1203, _____ presented Aibak with war booty, including 20 captured elephants, jewels, and cash
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, the Ghurid commander Bakhtiyar Khalji subjugated the petty Gahadavala chiefs in eastern Uttar Pradesh and the Bihar region. After his Bihar campaign, which involved the destruction of Buddhist monasteries, Khalji arrived in Badaun to greet Aibak, who had just concluded his successful campaign at Kalinjar.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak had purchased _____ sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave Iltutmish, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom. Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to 1203, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of _____ after his defeat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to 1203, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of Gujarat after his defeat. He was later killed as a subordinate of the Chaulukya king Bhima II when Aibak invaded Gujarat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In 1192, he took control of _____ and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1192, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local _____ ruler as a vassal
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal. In 1193, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In 1193, he deposed the _____ ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal. In 1193, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi.
